newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil weak, supply grows more.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil weak, supply grows more.

text.p: NWE high and low sulphur fuel oil prices were weaker on Wednesday as more supply loomed from across the Atlantic and from Russia, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $96.50 and $97 fob ARA but cargoes were quieter. Utility numbers were pegged at $92 cif NWE but dealers were unsure whether these bids were solid.
The last deal heard done was the sale of some 1.015 sg material out of Lavera to an Irish utility at $83 fob Med.
But more fresh tanker fixtures brought material into the region, with one 80,000 tonner and possibly another smaller cargo loading in the Americas in mid month with high sulphur.
Russians remain well supplied, especially Klaipeda E-4.

Low sulphur fell too. Swaps for March traded as low as $98.50 fob NWE before rising by around a dollar, and a trader was seen bringing 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil from the Caribbean to Europe. This was expected to cover a tender requirement in Turkey.

A refiner in the U.K. was heard to have sold late Tuesday a 45,000 tonne low sulphur cargo to a trader at approximately the quoted fob high. Another refiner in the U.K. was heard to have sold low sulphur barrels late on Tuesday to a trader, but price details were not immediately known.
